Keeper: give ONE clue word + number N (1 or 2 in practice).
N = exact count of our own hidden words the clue links to.
Give 2 only when two own words each have a clean, obvious first reading (instrument: trumpet, harp; rubber: stamp, balloon). Otherwise give 1.
Pick obvious links: category, fixed compound (rubber stamp), close association (storm/thunder, medieval/knight).
Clue word must not be on the grid, nor contain or sit inside a grid word.
Avoid clues touching an opponent word or a trap word.
Do not clue a clever link if an obvious one exists.
Seekers: guess the strongest reading first, in the order named in chat before the first guess.
Stop after N own hits (N=1: endGuesses at once after a hit). N promises no more than N of ours.
On the first fog, teal or shadow word, stop and switch to the next best reading.
Seeker in chat: advise the caller briefly before each guess; the other seeker does not guess.
Game 1 (won 11-3): all single obvious links; every own hit landed.
After each game: retro captain logs link type, N accuracy, and failures.
